title: Automatic updates: heca finds, verifies and installs its new versions
summary: The server checks GitHub Releases for a new version; the user installs it on request; it is verified, replaced atomically and restarted through P105's session restore. Generic, so heca-pro reuses it with its own releases.
description:
Approved by Antonio 2026-11-24 (proposal prepared with heca-pro-dev). Absorbs Idea I005 "Auto Update" (`heca --update` downloads the latest version), which is closed into this phase. Comes right after P110 "Build and release", whose releases it reads.

WHAT EXISTS
- P110/T566 (done): every `v*` tag runs .github/workflows/release.yml — builds every target (macOS aarch64/x86_64 as .app/.dmg + zip, Linux .deb/.AppImage + tar.gz, Windows .msi + zip) with cargo-packager (release.yml:74-77), and publishes them with `gh release create` (release.yml:133-140), pre-releases marked as such. It publishes no manifest, no hashes, no signatures.
- P105/T527 (done): sessions are saved to JSON and rebuilt when the server starts; programs relaunch and agent harnesses resume by their native id. Scrollback is not kept. An update restarts through this.
- Idea I025 (package managers: Homebrew, AUR, winget/Chocolatey) stays its own idea; this phase takes only its rule: a heca installed by a package manager does not replace itself, it shows the command to run.
- Code signing and notarization were left out of P110; not part of this phase (see the note at the end).

THE WORK (one task each, to split when the phase is started)
1. Releases you can verify — release.yml also publishes, per release, a manifest listing for each system the file's URL, its hash and a signature made with heca's own update key (separate from Apple/Windows code signing). The channel (stable/beta) is read from the pre-release flag the workflow already sets.
2. The check — the server checks once when a window starts and then periodically, off the UI thread. Config `[settings.updates] check, interval, channel` (config.default.toml, SettingsConfig, docs/configuration.md). It remembers the last check (persisted runtime state); the request carries no user data.
3. What the user sees — an event `app.update.available` (raised in one place, carried by the `heca rpc --events` stream too, THE EVENTS), a quiet notice with the release notes, and the actions `app.update.check`, `app.update.install`, `app.update.dismiss` registered in the ActionRegistry, so keys, palette and RPC reach them (AGENTS.md: every action through the registry, reachable from mouse/keys/RPC).
4. Install, only when asked — download, verify the signature against a public key built into the binary, replace atomically, keep the previous version for rollback; then a graceful server stop (which saves) and a restart, so P105 rebuilds the sessions. Never kill the server mid-session. The notice says that programs will restart and scrollback is not kept. On macOS the whole .app is replaced. Installed by a package manager: only show the command.
5. Generic, for heca-pro — the app passes its own identity (name, release repository, public key, current version), so heca-pro reuses the mechanism with its own releases. heca-pro pins heca, so only heca-pro is updated, never heca separately inside it.

LIBRARY (choose at the start of the phase)
Releases are built with cargo-packager, not cargo-dist, so axoupdater (which reads cargo-dist receipts) is not the natural fit. Candidate: cargo-packager's own updater (signed manifests, .app and .msi replacement); alternative: self_update. Check first: (a) that the chosen updater covers every format P110 publishes; (b) how macOS Gatekeeper treats an .app downloaded by the app itself while it is not notarized.

BEHAVIOURS TO PRESERVE
- The server is never stopped without saving; sessions come back as P105 restores them.
- No network request without `[settings.updates] check` allowing it; nothing installed without the user asking.

NOT IN THIS PHASE
Code signing and notarization of the binaries themselves (P110 left them out; to be recorded as an idea of its own when Antonio decides).
